The implementation instead runs a full base64 cleanup/decode on its input first, so feeding it raw bytes gives wrong results: Decode("abc") returns "i\uFFFD" (base64-decodes "abc") instead of "abc", Decode("hello world") returns garbage, and raw bytes that are not base64 characters are silently dropped (Decode("\xE8\xA0") and Decode("\xED\xA0\xA0") return "" instead of one and three U+FFFD). A 5613-case randomized comparison against Node found 449 mismatches, all of this kind.

The base64 cleaning loop diverges from Node for non-ASCII input. Node converts the string one byte per UTF-16 code unit (low byte) before base64-decoding, so U+0141 (\u0141) acts as 'A' and U+013D acts as '=' (stopping the decode); this implementation drops such characters instead.
